summary: Lighthouse on a Staten Island bluff above Raritan Bay: rubblestone tower 1828, brownstone tower 1864, discontinued 1922, now the Mount Loretto Unique Area.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1828 is the first light, with a rubblestone tower (archive; LighthouseFriends). 1864 is the present brownstone tower (LighthouseFriends). Both dates stand for different structures.

LighthouseFriends gives a third-and-a-half-order lens in 1857 and a fourth-order lens from 1890. The archive gives reflectors later replaced by a fourth-order Fresnel, with 1857 as the installation year. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: 1) Name: the Board's reports print 'Princess Bay' (the Bulletin index: 'Princess Bay light station'); same station on Staten Island. 2) OCR: the 1918 Bulletin p.45 passage was checked on the page image on 2026-10-27: 'At Princess Bay Light Station the dwelling shook considerably, and 18 panes of glass were broken out of the dwelling and the plastering in one room cracked.' The dwelling damage is confirmed; the story names the station as the Bulletin does. The index p.31 entry is clean. 3) The 1893 ice entry is OCR'd 'i(!e' and 'dur- ing'; the story reads it as ice. 4) Focal height: the archive gives 103.5 ft above mean high water (31.5 m, used here); the record's 27.1 m (ENC) is not matched. Not changed. 5) Current characteristic: the record's 'Q G' is not checked against a light list; LighthouseFriends gives a white flash every five seconds from 1890 and does not give the current characteristic. 6) Tower dates: the archive gives tower established 1828; LighthouseFriends gives the first rubblestone tower 1828 and the present brownstone tower 1864. The 1864 date is used for the present tower. 7) Harriet Riell (1848-1849) is a principal keeper in the archive and LighthouseFriends; no source explains her appointment, and none is inferred. 8) David Tuthill: archive 'at least 1843-1845'; LighthouseFriends 'David Tuthill, Jr.' 9) LighthouseFriends anecdotes not checked against primary sources: Rawson and Jackson, Bedell's daughter, the 1916 visit, the 1926 auction, the 1953 lease, the 1999 purchase and the 2006 renaming. They are reported as LighthouseFriends' account. 10) LighthouseFriends also tells of a child who lived with the keeper's family in 1920 (from a 1920 newspaper). Not used: a private person and not needed. 11) Chronicling America search 'Princes Bay' with 'lighthouse' (1840-1925, New York papers) returned unrelated pages; not used. 12) Not checked: NRHP status; any Board report before 1891 (the corpus starts there), so the 1828 and 1857 lens facts rest on the archive and LighthouseFriends. 13) Wikipedia read for leads only; nothing in this file cites it. 14) Fact-check 2026-10-27: 'harbor approaches' had no source and was replaced by LighthouseFriends' wording on the 1828 sites; 'leased' and 'orphanage' were reworded to LighthouseFriends' terms; the 1916 visit is now described as a reporter accompanying Inspector Yates.
